reforms.description: Canada established the National Health Research and Development Programme (NHRDP) in the early 1970s to conduct research on health delivery mechanisms, analyse innovative funding and delivery mechanisms, evaluate health care and health promotion programming, and assess health outcomes. The programme has been complemented by several provincially funded pilot schemes to improve community-based care and health promotion.
reforms.package_name: Health Systems Research and Evaluation Infrastructure
reforms.component_name: National Health Research and Development Programme
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Health systems research and evaluation improves the efficiency and effectiveness of health care delivery, reducing waste and improving health outcomes, which supports long-term productivity and human capital.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states NHRDP was 'created in the early 1970s' and 'conducts research', indicating active implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral research programme with structured mandate and provincial coordination, but not a system-wide structural reform.
reforms.source_quote: The mandate of the National Health Research and Development Program (NHRDP) likewise encompasses, inter alia, analysing innovative funding and delivery mechanisms, as well as the evaluation of health care and health promotion programming in terms of producing health.

reforms.description: Canada established the Canadian Co-ordinating Office on Health Technology (CCOHTA) in the late 1980s to encourage appropriate use of health technology through research and evaluation infrastructure assessing the effectiveness and appropriateness of medical technologies.
reforms.package_name: Health Systems Research and Evaluation Infrastructure
reforms.component_name: Canadian Co-ordinating Office on Health Technology
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Health technology assessment infrastructure improves allocation of health resources by identifying effective technologies, reducing inefficient spending and supporting better health outcomes.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states CCOHTA was 'established in the late 1980s', indicating implementation by the survey period (1993).
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant establishment of a dedicated research infrastructure for health technology assessment, but narrower in scope than a system-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: Technology assessment has also received attention in the late 1980s, with the establishment of the Canadian Co-ordinating Office on Health Technology (CCOHTA). Its goal is to encourage the appropriate use of technology via the collection, analysis and dissemination of information concerning the effectiveness and cost of competing technologies.

reforms.description: The Canadian government increased tax credits for R&D, already generous by international standards, and announced its intention to streamline delivery of and access to R&D programmes and services in the December 1992 Economic and Fiscal Statement and April 1993 Budget.
reforms.package_name: R&D Tax Credit and Programme Streamlining
reforms.component_name: R&D tax credit expansion and programme streamlining
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased R&D tax credits lower the cost of private R&D investment, incentivising firms to undertake more innovation and development activity, which supports productivity growth and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states the government 'announced its intention' in the April 1993 Budget, indicating announcement but not yet implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant increase to an existing major instrument (R&D tax credits) combined with programme streamlining, but announced rather than yet implemented.
reforms.source_quote: In its December 1992 Economic and Fiscal Statement, and again in the April 1993 Budget, the Government provided additional support to Canadian corporations undertaking R&D. At the same time, it announced its intention to streamline delivery of and access to R&D programmes and services.
